observations: Photo 0 shows a matte black game console consistent with the PlayStation 4 Slim design.
Two retail boxes for 'DUALSHOCK 4' controllers are positioned behind the console.
The text 'PS4' and 'DUALSHOCK 4' is legible on the controller packaging in photo 0.
A watermark 'POSTED ON JIJI DERA NWOYE' is visible on the image.
No cables (power, HDMI, or charging) are shown.
The console is not shown powered on or connected to a display.

claims.evidence: Requires a photo of the system software version and the home screen showing installed titles.

claims.claim: comes with two brand new pads
claims.evidence: Boxes are shown, but the controllers themselves are not visible out of the box to verify condition or authenticity.

risks.risk: The console may have a faulty HDMI port or internal hardware failure (BLOD).
risks.proof: A video clip of the console booting to the PlayStation home screen.

risks.risk: The console might not be 'hacked' (jailbroken), which is a high-value feature in this market.
risks.proof: A photo of the 'System Information' screen showing a firmware version of 9.00 or lower.

risks.risk: The controllers may be third-party clones rather than original Sony DualShock 4 pads.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the stickers on the back of the controllers.

risks.risk: The internal hard drive capacity is unknown.
risks.proof: A photo of the 'Storage' menu in the system settings.

proof_requests: Video of the console powering on and reaching the main menu.
Photo of the 'System Information' screen showing the software version.
Photo of the 'Storage' screen showing the HDD capacity.
Photos of the back of the controllers showing the model stickers.
Photo of the model and serial number sticker on the console.
response.reason: The item is identified as a PS4 Slim. It is priced at its worst case as a non-functional, unhacked 500GB unit until the seller provides proof of functionality and the jailbreak status.
